statements.t: All comments concerning our expectations for future revenues and operating results are based on our forecasts for our existing operations and do not include the potential impact of future operations or acquisitions.
The redemption is expected to be funded with borrowings under our revolving credit facility.
We intend to pay the distributions on November 23, 2026 to common unitholders and OpCo common unitholders of record as of the close of business on November 16, 2026.
We will pay a cash distribution on the Series A preferred units of approximately $2.5 million for the quarter ended September 30, 2026.
We intend to pay the distribution subsequent to November 5, 2026 and prior to the distribution on the common units and OpCo common units.

To date, we have not experienced a material adverse impact to operations or the consolidated financial statements as a result of these conflicts; however, we will continue to monitor for events that could materially impact us.
It is uncertain at this time to what extent such changes in regulations and tariffs will impact our business.

Our historical financial condition and results of operations may not be comparable, either from period to period or going forward, to our future financial condition and results of operations, for the reasons described below.

Acquisitions are an important part of our growth strategy, and we expect to pursue acquisitions of mineral and royalty interests from third parties, affiliates of our Sponsors and the Contributing Parties.
Accordingly, we can give no assurance that our current or future acquisition or investment efforts will be successful or that our strategic asset divestitures will be completed.
Although we expect the acquisitions and investments we make to be accretive in the long term, we can provide no assurance that our expectations will ultimately be realized.
We will not know the immediate results of any acquisition until after the acquisition closes, and we will not know the long-term results for some time thereafter.
The risk that we will be required to recognize impairments of our oil and natural gas properties increases during periods of low commodity prices.

With respect to future quarters, the Board of Directors intends to continue to allocate a portion of our cash available for distribution on common units to the repayment of outstanding borrowings under our secured revolving credit facility and may allocate such cash in other manners in which the Board of Directors determines to be appropriate at the time.

We do not currently intend to (i) maintain excess distribution coverage for the purpose of maintaining stability or growth in our quarterly distribution, (ii) otherwise reserve cash for distributions or (iii) incur debt to pay quarterly distributions, although the Board of Directors may do so if they believe it is warranted.
The redemption is expected to be funded with borrowings under our secured revolving credit facility.
We estimate that a portion of our quarterly distributions will constitute a non-taxable reduction to the tax basis of unitholders’ common units.

We currently believe that the portion that constitutes dividends for U.S. federal income tax purposes will be considered qualified dividends, subject to holding period and certain other conditions, which are subject to a tax rate of 0%, 15% or 20% depending on the income level and tax filing status of a unitholder for 2026.
